concerns.text: Task T001 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but creates the project root directory and sub‑folders. Parallel execution with other `[P]` tasks that also write to the same filesystem (e.g., T002‑T004) can cause race conditions and directory‑creation conflicts. This task should not be labeled `[P]`.
Task T002 is marked `[P]` yet writes `requirements.txt`, a file that may be concurrently accessed or overwritten by other setup tasks (T001, T003, T004). The `[P]` tag is unsafe.
Task T003 is marked `[P]` but creates a `.gitignore` in the same project root. Concurrent writes with other `[P]` tasks can lead to nondeterministic file content. Remove the `[P]` tag.

Task T004 is marked `[P]` while it creates a virtual environment and installs packages, which modifies the filesystem heavily. Parallel execution with other `[P]` tasks is unsafe; the tag should be removed.

Task T005 is marked `[P]` but depends on the successful completion of T001‑T004 (environment) and produces `data/raw/` which is later consumed by T006. It cannot be safely run in parallel with its consumers; the `[P]` tag is incorrect.

Task T006 is marked `[P]` yet it consumes the raw data produced by T005 and writes `data/derived/implicit_failure_subset.jsonl`, which is a prerequisite for T007 and the agents. Parallel execution could cause missing input; the `[P]` tag must be removed.
Task T007 is marked `[P]` but reads the file generated by T006. It cannot be parallel‑safe with its producer; the `[P]` tag is invalid.

Task T008 is marked `[P]` yet the augmented agent (T009) and runner scripts (T010) depend on the existence of the baseline implementation. Parallel execution with those consumers is unsafe; remove `[P]`.
Task T009 is marked `[P]` but requires the failure‑signature index created by T007. It must run after T007; the `[P]` tag is inappropriate.
Task T010 is marked `[P]` while it invokes both agents (baseline and augmented) which depend on T008‑T009. It cannot be safely parallel with its producers; the `[P]` tag should be removed.
Task T011 is marked `[P]` but consumes the execution logs produced by T010. Parallel execution could lead to missing logs; the `[P]` tag is invalid.
Task T012 is marked `[P]` yet it depends on the output of T011. It must run after T011; the `[P]` tag is unsafe.
Task T013 is marked `[P]` but formats the report using data from T012 and resource metrics from T014/T015. It cannot be parallel‑safe with those producers; remove `[P]`.

Task T014 is marked `[P]` but is a utility used by the orchestrator T015. While it could be built independently, labeling it `[P]` suggests it may run concurrently with tasks that also import it, which is harmless, but for consistency it should not be marked `[P]` unless explicitly parallel‑safe.
Task T015 is marked `[P]` yet it orchestrates the entire pipeline, depending on all prior tasks (T001‑T014). It cannot be run in parallel with any of its producers; the `[P]` tag must be removed.

Task T016 is marked `[P]` but its unit tests import modules produced by many earlier tasks (loader, injector, indexer, agents). Running it in parallel with those producers could cause import errors; the `[P]` tag is inappropriate.
Task T017 is marked `[P]` yet it runs an integration test that executes the full experiment, requiring all prior artifacts. It must run after T015; the `[P]` tag is invalid.
Task T018 is marked `[P]` but documents the entire project, referencing artifacts produced throughout the pipeline. It should not be parallel‑safe with its producers.
